text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.2% today to $125.15, continuing a five-day losing streak that has dragged the stock down 5.6% since late September. The weakness reflects broader energy sector pressure: crude prices have pulled back meaningfully (U.S. oil at $96 per barrel, down from the mid-$100s just days ago), and policy uncertainty around potential diesel export restrictions—which Trump said he was "very seriously" considering—threatens to constrain U.S. fuel markets and refiner margins if enacted.

The stock is also feeling pressure from uncertainty around the Alaska LNG project, a major growth opportunity for the company. South Korea's president pushed back on committing to the venture today, even after the Trump administration announced up to $200 billion in broader Korean investment, signaling that a key financing partner remains noncommittal on this capital-intensive undertaking.
